newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off on profit-taking, technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off on profit-taking, technicals.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower Thursday after a lack of buying interest at slimly firmer levels sparked late session profit-taking on thin volume.
"I think it had more to do with lack of buying interest on a small amount of volume than anything else. We then ran some sell stops below $20.00," said a New York crude dealer.

June crude ended 30 cents a barrel lower at $19.91 after being a few cents higher within a $20.21 to $20.25 price range most of the day. On the charts, technicians had been predicting June crude to break out of a bearish wedge formation on the spot continuation chart.
The wedge formation on the spot chart branched off from the April 22 session low and session high, and Thursday's breakout would signify an optimal two-thirds of the move.
Industry events in Houston had drawn dealers away from the market, thinning out trade and undermining the significance of the late session sell-off, dealers said.
June heating oil finished off 0.59 cent at 54.33 cents a gallon while June gasoline ended 0.22 cent up at 62.63 cents a gallon.
"There was a lot of buying interest in the gasoline crack spread," said a New York dealer.

The dealer noted gasoline prices were undergirded generally by tighter refomulated gasoline (RFG) supplies in RFG's primary market of the U.S. Northeast compared to a year ago just as the U.S. approaches its summer driving season.
